name: Roar of Resistance
oracle_text:
Creature tokens you control have haste.
Whenever one or more creatures attack, you may pay {1}{R}. If you do, creatures attacking your opponents and/or planeswalkers they control get +2/+0 until end of turn.
blocked_sentences: Whenever one or more creatures attack, you may pay {1}{R}. If you do, creatures attacking your opponents and/or planeswalkers they control get +2/+0 until end of turn.

needs.what: a selector key matching a creature attacking an opponent of the ability's controller OR a planeswalker such an opponent controls (not a battle, not the controller or the controller's planeswalkers), any creature's controller -- e.g. `attacking_player: "opponent"` widened by an `or_planeswalkers: true` flag that also accepts attackers whose combat.attacking_permanent is a planeswalker controlled by an opponent. Same need as Soul Snare's gap (attacking_you_or_your_planeswalker), mirrored to the opponent side
needs.why_existing_wont_do: The trigger is fine (`you_attack` with `controller: "any"`, as Duelist's Heritage writes it, then `may` with `pay: {"mana": "{1}{R}"}` wrapping a `pump`), and the first sentence is a `grant_keyword` static with `is_token`. But the pump's objects cannot be said: `attacking_player: "opponent"` deliberately excludes creatures in combat.attacking_permanent, so it drops attackers aimed at opponents' planeswalkers; `attacking: true` is a bare boolean and would also pump an opponent's creatures attacking you; `creatures_attack_player` with `defending: "opponent"` binds exactly the right attackers but fires once per defending opponent, so in a pod you would be asked to pay {1}{R} once per attacked opponent instead of once per attack, and it would not fire at all on an attack aimed only at you
